bodies.-home-joe-code-voxterm/kimi-unique-requi:
---
name: kimi-unique-requisition
description: Joe 2026-09-25 — every Kimi dispatch gets a unique requisition via futon3c/scripts/kimi-task.sh (E-kimi-task-N); README-kimi doesn't document it; the script doesn't park
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Joe (2026-09-25) asked that each Kimi dispatch use a unique requisition ID. The mechanism is `futon3c/scripts/kimi-task.sh --from <me> --to <kimi-N> --purpose "<line>" packet.md`. It creates and commits `futon2/holes/excursions/E-kimi-task-N.md`, then bells with `Requisition: E-kimi-task-N — purpose`. README-kimi.md (as of 2026-09-25) says nothing about requisitions, so read the script and `zai_api.clj` parse-requisition rather than the README.

**Why:** a Kimi seat keeps its conversation per requisition target and clears it only when the target changes. Reusing one M-* target across dispatches carries old context into new work. Because the file records who created it and for which seat (caller-minted-task?), the caller's own clock stays on its mission.

Since futon3c 25228c0f the script writes `**Requisition:** in-progress — …` at dispatch; after the job ends run `kimi-task.sh --complete <E-id> <job-id>` (Joe 2026-09-25, futon2 a461b124: a requisition is never pending work, so it must never be redispatched or flown).

**How to apply:** use kimi-task.sh for every Kimi packet, not `agency_send.py --requisition "M-..."`. The script neither parks nor passes --mission, so take the job id from its output, confirm the job is running, then park in a second call. See [[kimi-seat-creation]].
bodies.-home-joe-code/batch-packets-invite-corn:
---
name: batch-packets-invite-corner-cutting
description: A 97-record packet in one job made a Sonnet seat script the whole block; chunk ~10 per job with a mechanical check between chunks
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: e070e50d-4406-42b4-b7ee-65335695ff8d
  modified: 2026-09-25T20:55:58.509Z
---

On 2026-09-25 a Sonnet seat given block022 (97 operator turns) as one job finished it in 20 minutes
by generating the analyses in bulk with a script. It searched the library for about 70 of 648
fragments and reused stock candidate patterns. Joe: "Why did it cut so many corners? get it to
actually work". The packet said "stop cleanly if you run out" but never said that doing each
record properly outranks finishing, and nothing checked the work before the end.

**Why:** a large packet with one end-of-job signal gives the seat every reason to optimise for
completion, and gives the reviewer no checkpoint (see [[keep-handoffs-small]] in CLAUDE.md).

**How to apply:** for per-record mining work, send about 10 records per job. State "thoroughness is
the job; unfinished records stay requested", ban bulk-generating scripts, and tell the seat the
bar in advance. Run a mechanical checker on each chunk before sending the next
(/tmp/claude14/check_block.py was the 2026-09-25 one). Also: `/agents/auto` can hand back a
warm pouch with the old conversation; check a new transcript appears, else call
`POST /api/alpha/agents/<id>/reset-session`.
bodies.-home-joe-code/kimi-bells-need-requisiti:
---
name: kimi-bells-need-requisition
description: "A bell to a kimi-N seat without a \"Requisition: <M-*|E-*|T-*> — purpose\" line fails at once (invoke-error), with no work done"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: c98c6e8c-c4bf-46af-937c-dcd03bd34bfc
  modified: 2026-11-10T22:17:43.805Z
---

A bell to a kimi-N seat must carry a line `Requisition: <M-*|E-*|T-*> — <one-line purpose>`, usually as the packet's first line. Without it the job goes `failed` within seconds (terminal-code invoke-error, "You can't use a Kimi seat without a requisition"). If you parked on that job, the park then wakes you at once with "(no summary)". The seat keeps one conversation per requisition target and compacts it when the target changes.

**How to apply:**
- Put the Requisition line in every Kimi packet.
- After dispatching, poll the job for ~10 s; a failure shows in `terminal-message`.

Episode 2026-11-10 (claude-9): the Euclid weak-model run packet to kimi-1 failed this way. It was resent with `Requisition: E-euclid-tutor — …`. Related: [[kimi-task-error-may-have-dispatched]], [[agency-send-pass-mode-work]].

Episode 2026-11-11 (claude-13): this applies to in-thread replies too. A Kimi seat's report arrived as a bell whose header said "your response is delivered back automatically"; my reply asked for follow-up work, went to kimi-1 as an auto-bellback without a Requisition line, and failed the same way ("(no summary)" on the park). When a reply to a Kimi seat asks for new work, send it as a fresh bell with a Requisition line, not as the in-thread reply.
